3.  Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Second Quarter Treasurer’s Report
  State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within 30 days following each
  fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment balances. The purpose
  of the report is to inform you on a quarterly basis, the City’s cash and investment
  balances, the investment types, yields, and market values, and to ensure you that the
  City’s investments are in compliance with the City’s adopted Investment Policy.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt the resolution accepting the FY21-22 Second Quarter Treasurer’s Report.

4.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council of the City of Avalon
  made findings pursuant to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue
  this practice, it is required, that the City Council determine that the COVID-19 state of
  emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the City
  Council in deciding to continue to have teleconference meetings and that state or local
  officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social distancing in
  connection with COVID-19. and that as a result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in
  person would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these
  findings must be made every thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these
  findings at its upcoming March 1, 2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists

5.  Fourth of July Barge
  The City contracts a barge company annually to facilitate the Fourth of July fireworks
  show. Curtin Maritime expressed their interest in providing the barge service for the
  Fourth of July show and offered to match the lowest bid received by any barge company.
  Additionally, Curtin Maritime offered to only charge for the hard costs and donate any
  remaining monies back to the City of Avalon to support youth activities.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with Curtin Maritime to provide
  barge services for the 2022 Fourth of July fireworks display.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  Determine if the City Should begin the RFP/Bid Process for the City’s Transit System or
  extend the existing contract with Transportation Concepts.
  Transportation Concepts original contract was executed April 5, 2016 and was extended
  March 21, 2019, and again April 4. 2021, for a two-year term set to expire March 31,
  2023. The City Council has two options to consider: 1. Proceed with a request to issue a
  Request for Proposals for a consultant to assist City Staff to ensure all state and federal
  guidelines are incorporated into the RFP. After the RFP is complete, put the transit
  contract to bid. 2. Extend Transportation Concept’s contract an additional two-years.
  Recommended Action
  Provide Staff direction regarding pursuing an RFP for a new Transit Contract or extend
  the existing contract with Transportation Concepts.

REPORT SUMMARY: State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within
30 days following each fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment
balances, Attached is the Second Quarter Treasurer’s Report for FY21 -22.

The purpose of the report is to inform you on a quarterly basis, the City’s cash and investment
balances, the investment types, yields, and market values, and to ensure you that the City’s
investments are in compliance with the City’s adopted Investment Policy.

The report shows that all of the City’s funds are in compliance with its investment policy. In
general, operating cash is held in US Bank checking accounts and the excess cash is invested
in California’s Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF), less than 0.3% interest, and various
certificates of deposit (CD5), earning around 1.60% interest, as of December 31, 2021.

The unrestricted cash balance for the second quarter of 2021-2022 totaled $13.18 million, an
increase of approximately $6.45 million compared to December 31, 2020 and $2.19 million
compared to September 30, 2021. The increase in unrestricted cash can be partially attributed
to increases in transient occupancy tax (TOT) revenues, the City’s largest source of revenue.
Current fiscal year TOT revenues for overnight stays through November 2021 are up $1.53
million or 48.9% compared to the same months during the prior fiscal year. The unrestricted
cash balance also includes the first installment of American Rescue Plan funds totaling
$440,287. which were received by the City in July 2021, with the final installment expected
during the fourth quarter of the current fiscal year. Generally, unrestricted cash balances peak
during the first half of the fiscal year due to the seasonality of visitor-driven tax revenues and
the timing of major capital expenditures.

The cash balance in restricted accounts as of December 31, 2021 totaled S9.74 million, an
increase $286 thousand compared to the quarter ended December 31, 2020. The increase is
primarily attributable to budgeted contributions to the City’s landfill trust account totaling
$268,500, as well as unrealized investment gains in the City’s OPEB trust account and interest
income from LAIF investments for restricted funds.

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): At the January 4, 2022 City Council meeting, the City Council
of the City of Avalon (“City”) made findings pursuant to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet
remotely. To continue this practice, it is required, that the City Council determine that the COVID
19 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the
City Council in deciding to continue to have teleconference meetings and that state or local
officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection
with COVID-19, and that as a result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would
present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be
made every thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming
March 1, 2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. Newly enacted AB 361 provides an exception to these
procedures in order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including
the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in EQ N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings RequIred underAB 361

Under AB 361, the City Council can hold virtual meetings without providing notice of the City
Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes the determination that there is a

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social

  2. The City Council determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an

COVID-19 continues to present an imminent threat to the health or safety of members of the
public, and the Governor’s declaration of a COVID-19 emergency still exists. Although vaccines
are now widely available, many people in the State and County are still not fully vaccinated and
remain susceptible to infection. The disease can still spread rapidly through person-to-person

present in the State and County, the most predominant of which is the Delta variant. The City’s
economy is dependent upon visitors to the island, the presence of which, increases the likelihood
of transmission of the disease. Also, having members of the public attend council meetings at
locations where council members are in attendance due to their desire to avoid exposure to
COVID-19 poses an imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

Re-Authorization is Required Within 30 Days

The City Council made the findings listed above at its January 4, 2022 City Council meeting.
Consistent with the provisions of Government Code Section 54953(e), the findings must be made
every 30 days “after teleconferencing for the first time” under AB 361. Thus, if the City Council
desires to continue to meet remotely without having to post the location of each teleconference
location, the City Council must again find that the COVID-19 emergency still exists and that one
of the two following findings can be made: that state or local officials have imposed or
recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, or, that a
result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health
or safety of attendees.

It is recommended that the City Council make these findings.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City Council will
have to follow the Brown Act provisions that existed prior to the COVID-1 9 pandemic.

2022 City Council meeting.

SUBJECT:  Fourth of July Barge

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with
Curtin Maritime to provide barge services for the 2022 Fourth of July fireworks display.

REPORT SUMMARY: Though interrupted in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the City
contracts a barge company annually to facilitate the Fourth of July fireworks show.

Due to the high demand and a reduced number of providers for shows on the Fourth of July,
City Staff would like to secure a barge now.

On November 16 2021, Staff was contacted by a representative of Curtin Maritime expressing
their interest in providing the barge service for the Fourth of July offering to match the lowest
bid received by any barge company. Additionally, Curtin Maritime offered to only charge for the
hard costs (employee time and fuel) and donate any remaining monies back to the City of
Avalon to support youth activities.

Staff began soliciting bids by phone from barge service providers in late 2021. As of January
12, 2021 Staff had solicited bids from four companies; Foss! Sause Brothers. Pacific Tug, and
Curtin Maritime, but only received two responses! Pacific Tug and Curtin Maritime. Pacific Tug
came in first with a quote of 332,760 and Curtin Maritime, receiving that number through
Community Service Supervisor David Hart, matched the number in their quote, honoring the
offer to match the lowest quote.

Due to a breach of procurement procedures, on January 24, 2021! Staff resolicited bids from
the original four firms and two additional! Connolly Pacific and Avalon Freight. All firms had the
opportunity to observe what previous quotes had been received in the first bid solicitation. By
the time this report was authored! Staff received only two quotes  — Pacific Tug and Curtin
Maritime again. The estimate provided by Pacific Tug remained the same! $32,760, and Curtin
Maritime’s new estimate is $30000.

Staff recommend the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with
Curtin Maritime to provide barge services for the 2022 Fourth of July fireworks display. This
request is for barge services only. Staff will be coming back to the City Council to review the
total Fourth of July budget, seek approval of a firework contractor, determine the theme, and
activities schedule.
 If approved, this would be the first time the City of Avalon utilized Curtin Maritime’s barge
services for the Fourth of July fireworks show. In the past, Curtin Maritime donated the barge
services for the fireworks show provided to the City of Long Beach.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Enhance Recreational Opportunities.

FISCAL IMPACTS: The barge will cost $30,000. The City has a total budget of $50,000 for
the Fourth of July activities.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City would not
have a barge secured to launch fireworks for the Fourth of July Fireworks Display.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Provide Staff direction regarding pursuing an REP for a new
Transit Contract or extend the existing contract with Transportation Concepts.

REPORT SUMMARY: In 2015, the City of Avalon hired a consultant to assist in the
development of a Request for Proposals for the City’s Public Transit system which consists of
Dial-a-Ride and a Fixed-Route Service (The Garibaldi). The consultant fee in 2015 was
approximately $25,000. The process from development of the RFP to the award of the contract
was approximately twelve months.

Transportation Concepts original contract was executed April 5, 2016 and was extended
March 21, 2019, and again April 4, 2021, for a two-year term set to expire March 31, 2023.

The City Council has two options to consider:

1. Proceed with a request to issue a Request for Proposals for a consultant to assist City Staff
to ensure all state and federal guidelines are incorporated into the REP. After the REP is
complete, put the transit contract to bid.

2. Extend Transportation Concept’s contract an additional two-years and begin negotiations for
the contract extension to be brought back to Council for review at a later date.

Staff proposes option 2 for the following reasons:

  1. At the present time, City Staff is depleted due to COVID and extra duties are being
  assigned to multiple staff members to keep the City in compliance with a myriad of state
  and federal requirements.
  2. Transportation Concepts has been an excellent partner to the City and willingly adjusts
  fees (such as COVID) as needed.
  3. Transportation Concepts has provided excellent service to the community and
  collaborates well with the City.
